title: AXI Assertion Library: Trigger, Obligation, Context
description: Open a checker family to connect its sampling event to the exact protocol obligation, state that must be tracked, and common false-positive trap.

signals.name: Source VALID independence
signals.expansion: A source must not wait for READY
signals.description: The source of AW, W, AR, R, or B asserts VALID when it has a payload; it must not make that assertion conditional on the destination's READY.
signals.sampled: Every rising ACLK edge outside reset
signals.verificationNote: READY is allowed to wait for VALID. Do not write the rule symmetrically or flag a legal destination policy. Also check the interface rule that forbids combinational input-to-output paths.

signals.name: Stalled payload stability
signals.expansion: Hold VALID and the complete payload
signals.description: After VALID is asserted, it and every payload signal on that channel remain stable until an edge with VALID and READY HIGH accepts the transfer.
signals.sampled: Consecutive edges while VALID=1 and READY=0
signals.verificationNote: Qualify the payload by channel and reset. Checking only DATA while allowing ID, LAST, strobes, or response to change misses real corruption.

signals.name: AXI4 write response
signals.expansion: Accepted AW plus accepted final W precede BVALID
signals.description: For AXI4, a write response is generated only after the write address has been accepted and the final write-data transfer has been accepted.
signals.direction: AW and W events → B channel source
signals.sampled: Accepted AW, accepted W with WLAST, and BVALID assertion
signals.verificationNote: Do not require AW to arrive before W. AXI permits leading write data; the checker needs independent address and data state before permitting BVALID.

signals.name: LAST and beat count
signals.description: Count accepted data transfers and require LAST on, and only on, the final transfer declared by AxLEN.
signals.verificationNote: Advance the count only on a handshake. Backpressured VALID cycles do not create extra beats, and an error response does not cancel the remaining declared transfers.

signals.name: Burst address legality
signals.expansion: Size, length, alignment, wrap, and 4 KB
signals.description: Validate AxSIZE against the interface width, legal burst length/type encodings, WRAP alignment and length, generated byte lanes, and the rule that no burst crosses 4 KB.
signals.verificationNote: The 4 KB check uses the lowest and highest byte addresses, not merely the first and last presented beat addresses.

signals.name: Response ID and order
signals.expansion: Outstanding match plus per-ID issue order
signals.description: Every BID or RID identifies an outstanding request of the same channel type, and responses for repeated use of one ID return in original issue order.
signals.sampled: Accepted B beat or accepted R beat/RLAST
signals.verificationNote: A single associative entry per ID is insufficient because the same ID can be reused while multiple transactions are outstanding; use a queue per ID.

signals.name: Exclusive access restrictions
signals.expansion: Matched read/write attributes and monitorable span
signals.description: When exclusive accesses are supported, check total-byte alignment, power-of-two span up to 128 bytes, no more than 16 transfers, suitable attributes, and matching read/write request fields.
signals.sampled: Accepted exclusive read, exclusive write, and response
signals.verificationNote: EXOKAY is legal only for an exclusive transaction. Do not infer legality from AxBURST alone; the exclusive restrictions are a combined attribute and span check.

signals.name: Bounded progress contract
signals.expansion: Configured liveness, not universal AXI timing
signals.description: A project can require READY, response, or arbitration service within a configured bound under stated environment and fairness assumptions.
signals.direction: Product requirement → formal assumptions and assertions
signals.sampled: Request, accepted transfer, and completion windows
signals.verificationNote: Base AXI does not impose one finite READY or response-latency bound. Label the bound, reset behavior, arbitration assumption, and allowed backpressure explicitly.
